title: Ways to Make Array With Product
description: You are given a 2D integer array `queries` where `queries[i] = [n, k]`. For each query, return the number of different arrays of length `n` consisting of positive integers whose elements multiply to `k`, modulo `10^9 + 7`. Two arrays are different if they differ at any index.
hints: Factorize `k = p1^e1 * p2^e2 * ... * pr^er`. Distributing `e` identical copies of a prime into `n` distinct positions can be done in `C(n + e - 1, e)` ways (stars and bars), independently for each prime.

Precompute factorials up to `max(n) + 14` and their modular inverses via Fermat's Little Theorem (`fact[M]^(MOD - 2) mod MOD`) using fast exponentiation, plus a smallest-prime-factor sieve for O(log k) factorization per query.

examples.explanation: Any array of length 1 multiplying to k must be [k], giving 1 way for every query.
